newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: Two major Latin trade blocs seek free trade deal.
newsitem.headline: Two major Latin trade blocs seek free trade deal.

text.p: The two major trading blocs in Latin America will seek to join forces in a free-trade agreement, Venezuelan Foreign Minister Miguel Angel Burelli Rivas said on Monday.

He told Reuters in Cochabamba, Bolivia, where the Rio Group of Latin American nations will hold its 10th presidential summit on Tuesday and Wednesday, that the Andean Group and the Mercosur customs union were in talks to create a free-trade area.
"We are all going to join, the whole Andean community," he said. Peruvian Foreign Minister Francisco Tudela later said the two groups would formally announce their plans on Tuesday.
The Andean Group includes Venezuela, Colombia, Peru, Ecuador and Bolivia. Mercosur members are Brazil, Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay.

Burelli said Andean Group foreign ministers met earlier on Monday in this mountain city southeast of the capital, La Paz, to discuss their plans. The decision on joint entrance was taken after consulting with Mercosur nations, he said.
"Yesterday it was just Venezuela that was going to join (Mercosur) first, but now it has been decided that we are all going to do it," Burelli said.
Virtually all Latin American countries have cast aside protectionist and isolationist practices of the past and adopted regional economic integration as their watchword.

Chile negotiated a free-trade deal with Mercosur, and Bolivia has been negotiating a similar accord. Several other countries, including Mexico, Peru and Venezuela, previously expressed interest in a pact.
